label: Accessible coverage and the dependence-to-impossibility bridge
summary: Issue #2052. Selected loss yields the existing dependence-to-impossibility premise via soundness for the shared dependence primitive, accessible absence coverage and realization of being-without by an accessible witness. A three-world omission model exhibits a case where the effect drops after the chosen removal but persists in a farther accessible world. A separate normal/repair comparison reuses the matched AND/idle mechanisms and public-input clamp, which concerns public input absence only. None of these comparisons supplies an interpretation of the existence-fact labels in the strict-ground map.
blocker: OPEN: justify witness adequacy for real possibility and whether the same effect can persist under replacement in the sustaining scope. The dependence-to-strict-ground map still needs an independently interpreted existence-fact theory and its oriented edges.
